definition: Robotics is the branch of technology that deals with the design, construction, operation, structural disposition, manufacture and application of robots.
details: Robotics is related to the sciences of electronics, engineering, mechanics, and software.

explainer.lead: Robotics is the practical work of designing, building, operating, manufacturing, and applying robots. It brings together electronics, engineering, mechanics, and software to turn a robot from an idea into a working machine.

tiers.eli5: Robotics is like planning, building, and looking after a very complicated bicycle that can also follow instructions. You need to decide its shape, put its parts together, give it software, and make sure it works where people want to use it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat a robot as an interdisciplinary system rather than a software-only project. Work can span structural design, electronic and mechanical construction, software, manufacture, operation, and application, so choices in one area need to be checked against the whole machine.
tiers.paperLevel: Robotics can be summarized as: robotics = design + construction + operation + structural disposition + manufacture + application of robots. Its disciplinary basis includes electronics, engineering, mechanics, and software.

explainer.example: For a robot intended to move items in a workshop, engineers define its structure, build its mechanical and electronic parts, write its operating software, manufacture it, and then operate it for that application.

usedIn.name: Robot manufacturing
usedIn.detail: Covers the construction and manufacture of robots, including their structural disposition.

usedIn.name: Electronics engineering
usedIn.detail: Contributes electronic knowledge used in designing and constructing robots.

usedIn.name: Mechanical engineering
usedIn.detail: Supports the mechanical design and structural arrangement of robots.

usedIn.name: Software engineering
usedIn.detail: Provides software used in the operation and application of robots.

explainer.intuition: A robot is more than its body or its code: robotics covers the whole path from deciding what the machine should be to building, operating, manufacturing, and applying it.
howItWorks: Define the robot's design and structural disposition.
Construct it using relevant electronic, mechanical, and engineering knowledge.
Develop the software needed for its operation.
Manufacture the robot and put it into operation.
Apply the working robot to its intended task.
explainer.whyItMatters: The field connects several technical disciplines so that robots can progress from designs to constructed, operational, and useful machines.
misconceptions: Robotics is not only software; electronics, engineering, and mechanics are also involved.
Building a prototype is not the whole field: manufacture, operation, structural disposition, and application also belong to robotics.

nodes.label: Robot design

nodes.label: Construction

nodes.label: Application
